title: Coach Rick Bowness stepping away from Blue Jackets on day-to-day basis due to health
content:
Columbus Blue Jackets coach Rick Bowness is stepping aside on a day-to-day basis due to health concerns, Blue Jackets GM Don Waddell announced Saturday.

Bowness, 71, missed Thursday’s 3-1 loss to the Tampa Bay Lightning because he was “under the weather,” the club said. He wasn’t on the ice for practice Friday, either, as the Blue Jackets prepared for a home game on Saturday against the Philadelphia Flyers.

Assistant coach Don Granato, who assumed Bowness’ duties on Thursday, will remain in that position indefinitely. Waddell said Bowness will not travel with the team on Monday, as he will undergo further testing, but that he could join the trip later, depending on the test’s results.

“(Bowness) was here actually this morning. That’s a good sign. He was here for a little bit with the coaches. Until we know more, he’s listed like a player, day to day,” Waddell said.

This marks the second time in the past four seasons that Bowness has stepped away from his post to deal with a medical issue. In March 2024, while coaching the Winnipeg Jets, Bowness missed four games due to a “minor medical procedure.” Earlier that season, he missed a month of the season when he stepped aside after his wife, Judy, suffered a seizure.

It has been a star-crossed ride for Bowness in Columbus.

When he took over the club last January, after Dean Evason was fired, the Blue Jackets improved dramatically, becoming the hottest club in the NHL and playing their way back into the playoff race. A 19-3-4 run pushed them as high as fifth place in the Eastern Conference and second place in the Metropolitan Division, behind only eventual Stanley Cup winner Carolina.

Bowness was mentioned as a potential Jack Adams Trophy winner as coach of the year, even though he’d been behind the Blue Jackets’ bench for less than half a season. But a 2-8-1 finish to the season quelled that discussion and knocked the Blue Jackets out of a playoff spot, the sixth straight season in which they failed to advance to the playoffs.

Bowness was so frustrated by the Blue Jackets’ finish to the season, not to mention their half-hearted effort in a season-ending loss to Washington, that he lashed out at the players after the game, questioning their desire to win and vowing to change the culture in the dressing room. Bowness then signed a one-year contract to return to the team.

The players have not been receptive, and the losing that spoiled last season has dragged into this season. The Blue Jackets are 7-10-0 and have lost three straight games heading into Saturday’s game vs. the Flyers. The Blue Jackets have won only two games all season in regulation, tied with San Jose and ahead of only Vancouver (one).

Bowness, who holds the NHL record for most games coached (857), began with the Winnipeg Jets in 1989 and has also had stops with the Boston Bruins, Ottawa Senators, New York Islanders, Phoenix Coyotes, Dallas Stars and Winnipeg Jets.
